$comment: at-rule-no-unknown lists the Tailwind v4 at-rules because they are a CSS dialect a Payload project may legitimately be written in, not a carve-out for one repository's files. A project that uses no Tailwind never writes one, so the list costs it nothing, and a typo such as @theem still fails. The whole list is named rather than the subset one project happened to need: a missing entry sends the next project back to a config file it is not allowed to own, which is the wall this list exists to remove. import-notation follows for the same reason and is not a relaxation - Tailwind v4 mandates the string form (@import "tailwindcss"), so the url form the standard config wants cannot be written at all; the rule still enforces one notation, and the one it enforces is now the one that can exist. lightness-notation and hue-degree-notation are set to the NUMBER form rather than turned off, for the same reason the at-rules above are listed: ploaness admits Tailwind deliberately, and the generator most Tailwind projects theme with writes oklch(1 0 0) rather than oklch(100% 0deg). Demanding the percentage form failed every such project on CSS it never hand-wrote. One notation is still enforced; it is now the one that can actually exist.
